evidence: Caes. BG 7.22: nōtum atque ūsitātum (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 299: current, in general use, ūsitātus
terms.comment: “That’s normal” is ūsitātum est, or with a verb ita fierī solet. Back to normal: in prīstinum statum redīre (Caes. BG 7.54; see former).

terms.grammar: participle of soleō, used as an adjective
evidence: Liv. 3.38.9: quod solitum quicquam līberae cīvitātis fieret (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Augustan and later, not in Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short). With a comparative, solitō is “than usual”: solitō fōrmōsior, better-looking than usual.

evidence: Liv. 3.1.7: fēcit statim, ut fit, fastīdium cōpia

terms.gloss: made by the square, at right angles
evidence: Quint. 11.3.141: normālis angulus, a right angle (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. normal, ordinary, average (marked as a modern sense; Grosse 1846)
terms.comment: From norma, a carpenter’s square. The sense “normal” is nineteenth-century medical Latin (pulsūs frequentia normālis, Grosse 1846, in Morgan–Owens).

terms.gloss: handed down, conventional, the usual thing
evidence: Cic. Fam. 3.8.4: hoc trālātīcium est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly of what is handed on from one holder to the next, as a magistrate’s edict; so customary, ordinary, “the usual” (Lewis & Short, s.v. trānslātīcius).

phrases.latin: fēcit statim, ut fit, fastīdium cōpia
phrases.english: as normally happens, plenty soon bred boredom

phrases.latin: semel hic cessāvit et, ut fit, in scālīs latuit
phrases.english: once he played truant and, as boys will, hid on the stairs
